description: In this course, students investigate many forms of poetry, from the traditional (sonnet, villanelle, sestina) to the more recently invented (golden shovel, duplex, erasure). By studying canonical and contemporary poetry, students deepen their understanding of the relationship between form and content; by writing their own poems, students experience the ways in which formal constraints paradoxically produce freedom and surprise. At the end of the course, each student designs an original poetic form to share with the class, and then uses a classmates form to compose a new poem. Prerequisite: WRIT 120 or equivalent.
